floor.definition: At a fixed budget of 8 generations per problem, the floor on a row is the best of the published training-free selection rules below on that row's TEST problems (chosen after the fact per row, which favors the floor).
floor.F0: self-consistency, majority vote of 8 CoT samples (Wang et al. 2023; our sc-8)
floor.F1: DeepConf Mean@8: vote weighted by average trace confidence (Fu et al. 2025, arXiv 2508.15260, Eq. 2-3)
floor.F2: DeepConf Bottom-10% group confidence, top-90% filter, then weighted vote
floor.F3: DeepConf Lowest group confidence, top-10% filter (at N=8: the single most confident trace), then weighted vote
floor.F4: DeepConf Tail confidence, top-90% filter, then weighted vote
floor.F5: Self-certainty Borda voting, p=0.3 for N<=16 (Kang et al. 2025, arXiv 2502.18581, Eq. 4)
floor.F6: program-aided self-consistency, vote of 8 executed PAL programs (Gao et al. 2023; amendment 9's pal-8)
floor.our_settings: Token confidence C_i = -mean of the top-k log-probabilities with k=20. Our traces are 100-256 tokens, shorter than the paper's 2,048-token windows, so groups are overlapping windows of n=32 tokens (a trace shorter than 32 tokens is one group) and the tail is the last 32 tokens. Top-eta keeps ceil(eta*N) traces. Self-certainty per token = -(1/V) sum_j log(V p_j), averaged over the trace. Confidences are computed by one teacher-forced float32 pass over each stored path's generated tokens up to its first end of document.

search.space: Pools: CoT-8, PAL-8, CoT-4+PAL-4, prlm-0 family (prlm-0 and margin-branch paths 2-8), and the 16-generation pools CoT-8+PAL-8 and CoT-8+family. Aggregators: majority; vote weighted by each confidence (mean, bottom-10 group, lowest group, tail, self-certainty); top-eta filter with eta in {0.1, 0.5, 0.9} before the weighted vote; Borda with p in {0.3, 1.0} on each confidence; a cross-format agreement weight (an answer reached by both a CoT and a PAL trace has its weight multiplied by 2).
search.selection: Within each compute class (8 generations; 16 generations) select the rule with the highest pooled DEV accuracy (even problem indices of the 0.6B and 1.7B rows); ties to fewer mean tokens, then to the first in a fixed enumeration order written in the code before any score.
search.test: TEST = odd indices of 0.6B and 1.7B. Rows: Qwen3-0.6B-Base and Qwen3-1.7B-Base, GSM8K, the 400 problems of value.py.

claims.S1_primary: the selected 8-generation rule is a McNemar WIN over the per-row best floor rule on the pooled TEST problems, and a LOSS on no row
claims.S2: S1 clears the 3-point bar of VALUE_AMEND_2 on at least one row
claims.S3: the selected 16-generation rule against the best floor rule applied to the same 16-generation pool (F0-F5 on CoT-8+PAL-8), same test
claims.S4_sanity: each floor rule against F0 on all problems, reported (no claim: shows whether our implementation reproduces the published direction at this scale)
